transcript:
[Header]
Date: 2026-06-12 16:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Eleanor Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Orchid Head of ML), Lina Gomez (Orchid SRE), Tom Reed (Orchid CTO), Cindy Zhao (Orchid Product)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on sizing reserved GPU pool, defining burst strategy to Redwood hosted for peaks, and fallback policies to smaller/quantized variants. Agreed on concrete success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput targets, and cost envelope) and next steps to run a benchmark in staging.

Topics:
- Current LLM workload profile and sequence length distributions
- Concurrency targets and p95 latency SLOs
- Reserved capacity sizing and autoscale rules with burst to hosted
- Fallback model variants and canary policy for degraded capacity
- Security and data residency concerns for POC
- Timeline and deliverables for load test

Transcript body:
00:00:05 Eleanor: all right everyone thanks for joining — we got about an hour — Um quick roll call?
00:00:11 Samir: hi Samir here, Lina here, Tom and Cindy are on. audio a little spotty for Tom.
00:00:18 Eleanor: great, Marcus and Priya from my side, Marcus will run the technical bits. Goal today is to size the reserved GPU commit for your two-week POC and define autoscale/burst fallback rules.
00:00:32 Marcus: hi hi, quick agenda: workload profile, bench metrics, sizing, fallback/modes, and final checklist.
00:00:41 Cindy: perfect — we're very focused on minimizing latency for end users and keeping costs under our existing internal target — so tradeoffs matter.
00:00:48 Marcus: sure — maybe start with current traffic. Samir can you share typical qps, avg tokens, and peak windows?
00:00:55 Samir: yeah so our production calls are... uh two main features: short prompts (search rerank + snippet gen) avg 18 tokens, and long summarization up to 1,200 tokens but that only ~5% of calls. baseline traffic today is ~120 rps, peak around 420 rps during batch jobs or marketing pushes. concurrency per user thread is low, but aggregate concurrency is high during spikes.
00:01:25 Priya: when you say 420 rps is that across all endpoints?
00:01:29 Samir: yes across endpoints; rerank is most frequent — we also have scheduled bulk jobs at 3am causing sustained bursts.
00:01:36 Lina: to add, our 95th percentile latency target is 350 ms for short prompts, and 2s for long ones. Cost goal is to not increase inference ops spend more than 15% during the POC.
00:01:48 Marcus: ok good. For sizing we map to tokens/sec and model perf. Which model family are you testing?
00:01:55 Samir: we were planning to try the open-1.4 variants you recommended last week, plus a quantized 8-bit fallback. some references called it 'open-1.4-q8' or RW-1-4 in notes, so apologies if names are off.
00:02:08 Marcus: no worries, names often get munged by calendar notes. We'll benchmark a baseline FP16 variant and a q8 variant. For throughput numbers we need average sequence length histogram and request groups — can you share a sample day CSV?
00:02:20 Samir: yes, we'll attach that.
00:02:23 Marcus: mechanistically, for reserved capacity we recommend sizing for sustained baseline plus buffer: i.e., baseline sustained 120 rps -> token/s calc: 120 rps * 18 tokens = 2160 tokens/sec for short path; long path adds occasional load. A single A100-equivalent GPU in our tests handled ~9k tokens/sec for this model in FP16 under steady state with concurrency tuned. So a conservative reserved pool of 1-2 GPUs covers baseline with headroom.
00:02:50 Tom: does that account for KV cache memory and prefix caching? we do a lot of chat-like interactions with long context windows.
00:02:58 Marcus: good call — yes the throughput numbers assume KV cache hits for incremental tokens; very long sequences increase memory pressure and lower effective throughput. If your usage skews long, we factor that with per-session state sizing which could move you to 2-3 GPUs reserved.
00:03:14 Lina: for the POC we only need to cover 80% of expected peaks with reserved, and rely on burst to hosted for the extreme ~20%. we prefer that to buying extra reserved capacity.
00:03:23 Eleanor: that's a common pattern — reserved for predictable load, burst to hosted Redwood pools for spikes, with automatic fallback to quantized variants when hosted is saturated. we need to define the autoscale triggers and fallback order.
00:03:35 Marcus: rule proposal: keep reserved pool sized to baseline + 30% buffer. Autoscale policy: if queued requests > 60s or CPU/GPU util > 85% for >30s, allow burst to hosted up to X instances; then if hosted pool also saturated, fallback to q8 model variant with same routing.
00:03:51 Cindy: how do you estimate cost during burst? our finance team will ask.
00:03:55 Eleanor: we'll send a burst worksheet that models per-token cost across reserved vs hosted vs q8 fallback; you can plug in your traffic histogram. We'll also show cost delta if you choose to reserve 2 GPUs vs 1.
00:04:06 Marcus: one nuance: bursts to hosted preserve request ordering but may increase tail latency. for very latency-sensitive short prompts, we can configure a policy to prefer local reserved first and only burst non-critical endpoints.
00:04:19 Samir: can we do per-route policies? e.g., rerank stays local, summarization can burst.
00:04:23 Marcus: absolutely — Redwood routing supports per-route weight and per-model fallback lists. We'll propose a mapping: rerank -> local-only until util>90% then host fallback; summary -> allow immediate burst.
00:04:36 Tom: what about canary/failback if model version has quality regression on q8? we can't expose users to broken outputs.
00:04:42 Priya: we recommend a canary pass: route 5% traffic to q8 variants for short window and run quick evals comparing embed/semantic drift with a small prompt set. If metrics exceed threshold, auto-failback to FP16 or route to hosted FP16. Redwood Optimize can run these regressions during the POC.
00:04:59 Samir: how long to set the canary window?
00:05:02 Priya: for POC, 10-30 minutes is typical to get statistically useful signals for short prompts. we'll pick a small eval set you provide.
00:05:11 Lina: network/cloud egress for burst — data residency? Our data classification says customer PII cannot leave VPC without DPA. That might block bursting to hosted.
00:05:21 Eleanor: noted — if PII or regulated traffic can't leave your VPC, we can still support burst if you allow redaction or client-side de-ident; otherwise we'll need to run burst to a dedicated private pool (Redwood Dedicated) which is pricier. For POC we can scope a subset of traffic that is non-PII for burst tests.
00:05:39 Cindy: ok we'll identify a non-PII slice.
00:05:42 Marcus: another fallback is to run a smaller quantized model inside your private deployment; that keeps data in VPC but requires we provision extra reserve GPUs. Tradeoff between security and incremental cost.
00:05:53 Tom: what about pre-warming and cold-starts during sudden peaks?
00:05:58 Marcus: we do continuous batching and pre-warm policies. cold-starts are mostly a problem with auto-scaler bringing new nodes up; Redwood's burst uses a warm pool in hosted infra to reduce cold-start time to ~200-400ms for small models; larger models might be 600-1,200ms. For strict p95 350ms short prompt SLO we should ensure warm pool or route to reserved.
00:06:18 Samir: ok that means for rerank route we must keep warm pool local or require strict reserved.
00:06:22 Eleanor: yes. We'll enumerate per-route settings in the workbook.
00:06:26 Marcus: on metrics we will capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll also track model output quality deltas for canary.
00:06:36 Priya: for the benchmark runner we'll use a replay of your sample traffic with synthetic timing and interleaving. Marcus will send a script; we recommend run lengths of 30-90 minutes to capture variance.
00:06:47 Samir: what about session affinity? our application pins session state to a user, so if routed across different nodes we need sticky KV cache or it increases token costs.
00:06:56 Marcus: good point. We can enable session affinity on the routing layer for duration of a session, and Redwood's KV cache can be sharded. That reduces duplicated context transmission. sticky routing adds slight load imbalance but usually worth it.
00:07:08 Lina: okay, timeline — we'd like to run the POC load test week of 6/22 and have results the following week. Is that feasible?
00:07:15 Eleanor: yes, if we get the sample traffic and staging access by 6/16 we can run tests 6/22 and share results by 6/24. That fits a two-week POC cycle.
00:07:23 Marcus: action items: Marcus send bench runner, Eleanor send pricing/burst worksheet, Samir provide traffic CSV.
00:07:29 Samir: noted.
00:07:31 Tom: security docs — please send SOC2 summary and network diagram for private option.
00:07:36 Eleanor: we'll attach the SOC2 summary and our private deployment checklist.
00:07:40 Priya: small technical aside on fallback ordering: recommended order is reserved FP16 -> hosted FP16 -> hosted q8 -> local q8 (if private allowed) -> degrade to cached responses or partial result if all else fails.
00:07:53 Cindy: partial results would be acceptable only for batch jobs, not live user interactions.
00:07:57 Marcus: noted — we'll include an explicit degrade policy per route.
00:08:02 Samir: any recommended monitoring thresholds to avoid thrashing?
00:08:06 Marcus: yes — hysteresis is important: require nat > threshold for 30s and cool-down of 60s before reversing. Also use rolling 1-minute averages for utilization.
00:08:15 Lina: can Redwood show token-level cost in the console during POC?
00:08:18 Eleanor: yes, the Console shows token and per-model cost breakdown. We'll enable a 1-minute granularity dashboard for the load run.
00:08:26 Tom: latency vs cost question — our product folks will likely push for lower cost even if p95 slightly increases; how to surface tradeoffs quickly?
00:08:34 Eleanor: Redwood Optimize provides tradeoff sims: you can toggle quantization level and batching and see simulated cost and expected latency. For POC we'll run 2 axis experiments: FP16 vs q8 and batch size 1 vs 4. We'll share results in a spreadsheet.
00:08:47 Samir: what's the recommended reserved commit number again?
00:08:49 Marcus: baseline 1 GPU if your workload is short sequence heavy; 2 GPUs if long context sessions >200 tokens are frequent. Given your current histogram (18 tokens mostly, 5% long) I'd recommend 1 reserved GPU + hosted burst and local q8 fallback. That's the lowest cost path for a POC.
00:09:05 Cindy: what about autoscaling upper bound to prevent runaway cloud spend?
00:09:09 Eleanor: we can cap burst capacity and put hard spend guardrails; Redwood also supports per-hour spend caps that stop bursting beyond threshold.
00:09:17 Lina: good. We'll want that.
00:09:19 Samir: one more operational question — how do you test correctness/regression when falling back to q8? sometimes rerank order changes subtly and we can't accept that.
00:09:28 Priya: we'll configure automatic A/B eval on a small golden set of prompts and compare rerank NDCG or other metric you choose; exceed threshold --> auto-failback. We'll also log examples for manual review.
00:09:40 Samir: great.
00:09:43 Marcus: any blockers on our side?
00:09:46 Tom: only the data residency constraint for PII. We'll provide a non-PII traffic slice. Also we need finance to sign off on short-term burst budget — I'll loop them in.
00:09:56 Eleanor: excellent. To recap quick: reserved 1 GPU baseline, autoscale to hosted for spikes with cap, fallback order defined, canary plan for q8, bench runner and traffic CSV to be shared, schedule load-run week of 6/22.
00:10:12 Samir: yep.
00:10:14 Eleanor: ok we'll follow up with workbook and scripts. Marcus do you want to add any config specifics?
00:10:19 Marcus: I'll add a sample autoscale YAML and the routing table example showing per-route policies. I'll drop links in the email.
00:10:26 Marcus (later): Also note — if you want to test dedicated private burst (no data leaving VPC) we can scope a short Dedicated eval but that usually adds 2-3 days for provisioning.
00:10:36 Cindy: not for this POC. maybe later.
00:10:39 Tom: timeline on security docs?
00:10:41 Eleanor: we'll send within 24 hours.
00:10:44 Samir: okay thanks all.
00:10:46 [Crosstalk]
00:12:50 Eleanor: (summary) action items restated: pricing worksheet, bench runner, sample traffic, schedule test. Any other questions?
00:13:00 Lina: none.
00:13:02 Cindy: thanks.
00:13:05 Tom: thanks.
00:13:10 Eleanor: great meeting, we'll email notes + next steps.

[End of recording — remainder of the hour used for side technical clarifications between Marcus and Lina about per-node memory configs which are in Marcus' follow-up doc. audio faint for Tom around 00:22:00-00:25:00]
